agenda: Map Acme Freight's current dispatch process and the cost of late deliveries.
Explore live ETA needs and a practical Kestrel Dispatch pilot.
Resolve Tom's data migration concern and define the security review.
Confirm the approved budget, competitive timeline, decision process, and owners.

chapters.title: Acme's Dispatch Reality
beats: Elena describes 140 trucks across regional lanes, with dispatch still coordinated through spreadsheets and phone calls.
Tom explains how seven dispatchers copy status updates into separate sheets and lose time chasing drivers.
Elena says customers ask for live ETAs, and late deliveries currently surface only after a manual call.
Daniel and Priya separate late departures from inaccurate arrival predictions before discussing a solution.

chapters.title: A Pilot That Shows Value
beats: Priya proposes a two-week pilot on one regional lane, measuring ETA visibility, dispatcher time, and late deliveries.
Tom challenges a dashboard-only pilot because a dispatcher still has to use the live board during a real shift.
The group narrows the pilot to 20 trucks, two dispatchers, and one customer contact, with manual and Kestrel views side by side.
Elena wants a decision based on actual dispatcher use, not a polished sales demo.

chapters.title: Migration and Security Gates
beats: Tom objects that six years of inconsistent spreadsheet columns and customer codes make a full migration risky.
Priya says the pilot can import only active drivers, vehicles, and open loads after a sample mapping review, without moving old records.
Elena confirms Acme requires a security review before production access or customer-facing pilot data.
Daniel commits to sending the security packet tomorrow, and Priya and Tom agree to review a 50-row export by Friday.

chapters.title: Buying Decision and Next Steps
beats: Elena confirms a roughly $60,000 annual budget is approved and a selection is due by the end of next month.
Acme is evaluating two competing products; Elena will compare ease of adoption and credible live ETAs as well as price.
Daniel commits to a written pilot proposal and pricing by end of week; Elena will introduce Acme's security lead next week.
The group closes with named owners, a pilot gate, and no commitment to purchase before Acme sees results.
